title: Course Schedule
statement: There are numCourses courses, numbered from 0. Each pair [a, b] says you must finish course b before you can take course a. Decide whether it is possible to finish every course.

example.caption: Courses 1 and 2 each need the other, so neither can ever start. Course 0 is fine.

output.label: false: 1 and 2 are stuck in a cycle

idea.sentence: Keep finishing courses that have nothing left to wait for. If you run out of such courses before all are done, the rest must be waiting on each other in a cycle.

jargon.plain: How many arrows point into a node. Here: how many prerequisites a course still waits for.
A loop of arrows that leads back to where it started. Courses on a loop can never be started.
Repeatedly remove nodes with in-degree 0. It is a breadth-first search over a directed graph.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the course count, then the pairs, e.g. 4, [[1,0],[2,1],[1,2]]

compare.bruteLabel: Try every possible order (grows like n!, drawn as 2^n)
compare.optimalLabel: Queue pass over courses and pairs

rows.name: Try every order
rows.note: Check each ordering of the courses against all pairs.

rows.name: Kahn's algorithm
rows.note: Each course is queued once and each pair is looked at once. The lists hold every pair.

fast.takeaway: You never need to find the order. Peeling off free courses one by one either reaches everyone or gets stuck on a cycle.

stages.title: Build arrows
stages.note: For each pair add an arrow pre to course, and count each course's incoming arrows (in-degree).

stages.title: Seed the queue
stages.note: Every course with in-degree 0 has no prerequisites. Put them all in the queue.

stages.title: Finish a course
stages.note: Take the front course off the queue. It is done.

stages.title: Unlock courses
stages.note: Lower the in-degree of each course that needed it. Any that reach 0 join the queue.

stages.title: Count them
stages.note: If every course went through the queue, there is no cycle. Otherwise some are stuck.

edges.title: No prerequisites
edges.why: Every course starts with in-degree 0, so all go straight into the queue.

edges.title: Two-course loop
edges.why: Both courses wait for each other. The queue starts empty and nothing is ever finished.

edges.title: Cycle away from the start
edges.why: Course 0 finishes, but 1, 2 and 3 form a loop. Finishing some courses does not prove all can finish.

edges.title: Prerequisite on itself
edges.why: A course that needs itself has in-degree 1 forever, so it is never queued.

gotchas.text: The pair is [course, prerequisite], in that order. The arrow goes from the second number to the first. Swapping them still detects cycles but breaks any later ordering logic.
Array(n).fill([]) gives every course the same inner array. Use Array.from({ length: n }, () => []) so each course gets its own list.
queue.shift() is O(n) on big arrays. Walk a head index over a growing array, as here, to keep the loop linear.
Appending to a nil slice is fine, so next[pre] = append(next[pre], course) works on a make([][]int, n) with no setup. Reading a nil slice in range is also safe.

recap.key: Repeatedly finish courses whose in-degree is 0. If everything gets finished there is no cycle.
recap.complexity: Time O(n + m). Space O(n + m).
moves: Build next-lists and in-degrees from the pairs
Pop a course, lower the in-degree of what it unlocks, queue new zeros
Return whether the queue handled all n courses
